s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis
salient_findings: Recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb
key_facts: 56-year-old man
Four-year history of skin lesion on the right thumb
Partial amputation of the thumb in December 2016
Lesion reappeared at the distal aspect of the thumb stump in August 2017
No significant medical history
No medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion over the dorsum of the right thumb stump
Lesion is mobile over deep structures
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Metastatic workup included CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and a bone scan
Enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer with potential for local recurrence

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer with high risk of metastasis

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant skin cancer with potential for metastasis and poor prognosis

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Locally aggressive skin cancer with potential for recurrence

raw.rationale: The lesion's recurrence after partial amputation and the presence of metastatic disease, as indicated by the enlarged axillary lymph node, are more consistent with a aggressive skin cancer like squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely to metastasize and recur aggressively

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more rapid growth and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: Usually associated with a more irregular and pigmented lesion

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Characterized by a slower growth rate and less aggressive behavior
